title: Microburst Failure Inspector — compact overlay for rapid triage
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Design a compact overlay 'Microburst Failure Inspector' that surfaces minimal but high-leverage payload and retry insights for quick triage during short high-error episodes (microbursts). The overlay appears anchored to a selected request in the main console timeline and focuses on three lanes: quick-retry-summary, exemplar-payload-diff, and lightweight-error-taxonomy tags. It's intended for investigators who need to act in under 90 seconds without leaving the dashboard or opening a full debug panel.
comments: 2025-02-14 — Kickoff meeting notes: aligned on goals; opted for overlay instead of new pane to reduce navigation cost. PM suggested prioritizing network vs model errors filters.

2025-02-18 — Early wireframes uploaded to Figma (link: https://www.figma.com/file/example/microburst-inspector). Design exploration included compact charts (sparklines) and an expandable payload snippet with side-by-side diff.
2025-02-21 — Eng review: Victor Chen flagged KV cache privacy constraints for payload snippets; agreed to mask PII and require role-based reveal. Added security_review_required.

2025-02-24 — Prototype built in InVision; usability test with 5 engineers: median triage time reduced from 4m20s to 1m10s in study tasks. Notes: need clearer affordance for 'retry with backoff' action and rate-limit policy hints.
2025-02-27 — PM feedback: prefer single-click creation of a canary rollout from inspector when suspecting model variant regressions. Added 'create-rollout' microflow to next steps.
2025-03-01 — Design PR opened and linked to GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2987. Awaiting engineering implementation estimate.
next_steps: Finalize accessibility spec, confirm KV cache masking approach with security, workshop rollout microflow with PM and Eng, and hand off hi-fidelity Figma frames + interaction spec.
